By Ben Tan First Published: Thursday, 19 Nov 2026 10:49 AM MYT × Subscribe to Newsletter
 Subscribe ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 19 — Johor’s revenue is projected to exceed RM3 billion for the first time in the state’s history by the end of 2026, Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said today.
 He said the state’s revenue collection had already reached RM2.8 billion as of this morning, surpassing its original estimate for the year.
 “As of this morning, at the time of this presentation, Johor’s revenue collection has reached RM2.8 billion, equivalent to 110 per cent of the original estimate for this year.
 “Following this positive development, the state’s revenue is projected to exceed RM3 billion for the first time in history by the end of 2026,” he said while tabling the Johor Budget 2027 at the state legislative assembly at the Sultan Ismail Building in Kota Iskandar here.
 For 2027, Onn Hafiz said the state government projects revenue of more than RM3.076 billion, against estimated expenditure of more than RM3.074 billion.
 He said the figures would result in a surplus of RM2.328 million.
 The Johor Budget 2027, themed Johor Maju, Rakyat Sejahtera (Progressive Johor, Prosperous People), incorporates 284 commitments aimed at ensuring the state’s progress brings tangible benefits to Johoreans.
 Onn Hafiz said the commitments are structured under the Six Pillars of a Progressive Johor ( Enam Teras Maju Johor ), aimed at driving comprehensive development and improving the well-being of the people.
 “The increase in state revenue will be fully utilised to assist those who are truly in need.
 “This additional revenue will continue to be directed toward supporting the poor, orphans, persons with disabilities (PwD), the aged and as many Johoreans as possible who require assistance.
 “God willing, the government I lead will continue to work wholeheartedly, serving and caring for the people, regardless of their political background, race, or religion. We will serve everyone,” he said.
 For development expenditure, the state government plans to allocate RM1.53 billion, or 49.77 per cent of the total budget, next year.
 Onn Hafiz said the allocation, which accounts for nearly half of the budget, would fund improvements to public facilities used by Johoreans daily.
 “The RM1.53 billion development allocation represents more than a twofold increase compared to the RM600 million or 34.6 per cent allocated in 2023,” he said.
